transcript.text: my oven fan keeps going after ive turned the oven off, been about 20 mins now. is it broken??

No, your oven is likely not broken. In fact, this is a very common and normal feature of most modern ovens.

### Why does this happen?
The fan (often called the cool-down fan or convection cooling fan) continues to run after you turn off the oven to:
1. Cool down internal components: It helps dissipate heat from the heating elements, electronics, and control board to prevent damage.
2. Protect surfaces: It keeps the exterior of the oven cooler to the touch for safety.
3. Prevent residual cooking: It stops the oven from staying hot enough to continue cooking food inside.

### How long does it usually run?
• Typically, the fan will run until the internal temperature drops below a safe threshold (often around 100–150°F / 40–65°C).
• This can take anywhere from 10 to 30 minutes, depending on how hot your oven was and the ambient room temperature.
• Some ovens may run it for even longer if they were used at very high temperatures (e.g., self-cleaning mode or baking above 450°F/230°C).

### When should you be concerned?
You should only worry if:
1. The fan runs for more than an hour after turning the oven off.
2. You hear unusual noises (grinding, screeching) from the fan.
3. The oven itself feels excessively hot to the touch on the outside or door.
4. You see smoke or smell burning plastic/electronics.

### What you can do now:
• Wait it out: Give it another 10–15 minutes. It should shut off automatically.
• Check for a "Cool Down" indicator: Some ovens have a light or display message that says "Cooling" or shows a fan icon while the fan is running.
• Ensure ventilation: Make sure nothing is blocking the oven’s vents (usually at the back or bottom).

Bottom line: If it’s been 20 minutes and you don’t hear strange noises, your oven is likely just doing its job correctly. It will turn off on its own once it’s cool enough.
